name: mw-equilibrium-reproduction
title: Reproducing the MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium: rate crossing + turnover
question:
Does a direct, phenomenological implementation of the original theory of
island biogeography (MacArthur & Wilson 1963, 1967) reproduce its three core
claims — (1) species richness relaxes to the equilibrium S* where the
immigration and extinction rate curves cross, (2) richness tracks the analytic
S* = P*c/(c+e) across islands, and (3) species identity turns over while
richness stays constant?
hypothesis:
The mw_equilibrium composite colonizes each absent species at probability
c = colonization_base/(1+distance) and goes extinct each present species at
e = extinction_base*(ref_area/area)^area_exponent. Immigration I(S)=(P-S)c
falls with S, extinction E(S)=S*e rises with S, so richness must relax to and
fluctuate about S* = P*c/(c+e). Because colonization and extinction never stop,
the island keeps gaining and losing species at equilibrium (turnover), so gross
colonization+extinction events over a window vastly exceed the net change in S.
objective:
Over a log-spaced area gradient (12 islands, isolation fixed) and an 8-seed
ensemble, measure (a) the correlation between the ensemble-mean equilibrium
richness and the analytic S*, and (b) the turnover ratio (gross events / net
richness change) on a representative island, and render the rate-crossing
diagram, the approach-to-equilibrium trajectories, and the turnover curves.
description:
This study reproduces the ORIGINAL theory directly, as a counterpart to the
mechanistic Lotka-Volterra port used elsewhere in this investigation. The
MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess treats each species as present/absent and
draws colonization/extinction from the isolation- and area-dependent rates of
The Theory of Island Biogeography. A single run over an area gradient yields
the rate-crossing equilibrium, the approach to S*, and turnover at constant
richness — the three signatures of the 1967 monograph.

expected_behavior.name: equilibrium-tracks-theory
expected_behavior.en:
The ensemble-mean equilibrium richness per island tracks the analytic
S* = P*c/(c+e) closely across the area gradient (correlation near 1).
expected_behavior.rationale:
If the colonization/extinction process is implemented correctly, its
stationary richness must sit at the fixed point of I(S)=E(S); averaging over
seeds removes the single-realization noise so the fixed point is visible.

expected_behavior.name: turnover-at-equilibrium
expected_behavior.en:
Species identity turns over at equilibrium: gross colonization + extinction
events over the equilibrium window vastly exceed the net change in richness.
expected_behavior.rationale:
Turnover is the central dynamical prediction distinguishing the equilibrium
theory from a static species count — richness is a balance, not a fixed set.

behavior_tests.name: equilibrium-tracks-theory
behavior_tests.description: Ensemble corr(observed equilibrium S, analytic S*) must exceed 0.9.

provenance.note:
Measured eq_track_corr = 0.992 (12 islands, 8-seed ensemble, 400
generations, tail 25%). 0.9 is a conservative floor for "tracks theory".

behavior_tests.name: turnover-at-equilibrium
behavior_tests.description: Gross equilibrium events must exceed net richness change by >3x.

provenance.note:
Measured turnover_ratio = 15.5 on the representative mid-gradient island
(gross colonization+extinction / |net dS| over the tail window).

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Establishing that the mw_equilibrium process reproduces the rate-crossing
equilibrium and turnover licenses using it to measure the species-area and
isolation laws.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Rate crossing + approach to S* + turnover (12 islands, 8-seed ensemble)

conclusion:
The mw_equilibrium process reproduces the original theory: ensemble-mean
equilibrium richness tracks the analytic S* = P*c/(c+e) across the area
gradient (corr = 0.992), and species identity turns over strongly while
richness holds (turnover ratio ~ 15x). The simulation sits on MacArthur and
Wilson's crossing immigration/extinction curves. The emergent species-area
slope on this gradient is z ~ 0.12, in the low end of the empirical 0.1-0.35
band, partly because the large islands approach pool saturation.

turnover-at-equilibrium.detail: turnover ratio = 15.5 on the representative island (> 3).

findings.statement: The equilibrium model sits on MacArthur & Wilson's crossing rate curves: ensemble-mean richness tracks the analytic S* = P*c/(c+e) across the area gradient (corr 0.992), and species identity turns over ~15x the net change while richness holds.

turnover-at-equilibrium.detail: turnover ratio = 15.5 on the representative island (> 3).
